bench: Zero engine errors; 1 world; 52 records; the geometry table published as one observation artifact; threshold_share was 0.0078 (2 of 256 rules) on every row: the decoder-totality check passed (every encoding maps 16 genotypes to each rule). The rank-correlation primary is a new machine capability (states.spearman + primary type rank_correlation) exercised for the first time. Bench notes: (1) the exhaustive geometry of 4096 genotypes x 12 neighbours per encoding took 0.63 s for all 52 rows -- the cheap measurement that should precede any search comparison on a finite genotype space; (2) the hill climb's censoring at budget+1 (1289) compresses the slow tail; a larger budget would separate the censored scrambled rows (MISSING_TELEMETRY, minor).
disposition_note: Assay capable (direct 12/12 hits); over 13 encodings x 4 tables the parent's proxy (accessible variation) does not rank-correlate with efficiency (rho -0.23 vs -0.5 declared). Reported beside it, unpromoted: basin_share -0.59, greedy_path_len -0.59, deceptive_share +0.57 are the statistics that track this climber's efficiency.
landscape: On the block-output evaluator the threshold region is 2 of 256 rules (32 of 4096 genotypes under every total encoding). Direct: 38% of genotypes sit in a greedy basin of those 32 and the mean Hamming distance to the nearest threshold genotype is 3.25; balanced: 18% and 2.51 (closer on average, but the greedy paths are trapped: deception 0.69); scrambled: 10% and 3.42. Deceptive share is the landscape feature the parent's proxy missed: an encoding can hand the climber more distinct improving neighbours per step and still route most of them into local optima below threshold. Search efficiency followed the basin, not the neighbourhood.
science: Assay capable: the direct encoding hit the threshold in 3/3 search seeds on all 4 tables (median first hit 37-61 evaluations). PRIMARY (the parent's proxy): rho(accessible_variation, log first-hit) = -0.23 over 52 encoding x table rows against the preregistered -0.5; the machine candidate CAPABLE_NEGATIVE is accepted: accessible variation does not predict this climber's efficiency on this evaluator. The exhaustive geometry says why, and it separates the parent's puzzle cleanly. Balanced encodings have MORE accessible variation than direct (11.75 vs 9.00 distinct neighbour rules), more useful variation (5.14 vs 2.89 improving distinct rules) and a higher local improvement probability (0.44 vs 0.24), yet search 9x slower (median 413 vs 45 evaluations): their greedy BASINS of the threshold set are half the size (basin_share 0.18 vs 0.38), their deceptive share is higher (0.69 vs 0.44: genotypes with an improving neighbour whose best-improvement path ends below threshold) and their greedy paths are shorter (1.47 vs 2.30 steps: the climb stalls early). Scrambled encodings keep direct's local statistics exactly (accessible 9.00: a rule permutation cannot change neighbourhood multiplicities) and are the slowest (median 804; 11 of 24 rows censored at the budget) with the smallest basins (0.10) and the most deception (0.73). Across all 52 rows the statistics that rank-correlate with efficiency at |rho| >= 0.5 are the GLOBAL ones -- basin_share (-0.59), greedy_path_len (-0.59, longer sustained climbs go with larger basins) and deceptive_share (+0.57) -- while every LOCAL variation statistic is below |0.25| (useful_variation -0.12, local_improvement_prob -0.13). Exploratory: within a kind the correlations weaken (balanced n=24: local_improvement_prob -0.30 is the largest; scrambled: mean_dist_to_threshold +0.53, basin -0.44), so the between-kind difference carries most of the signal, and 'basin share' is the best single description of what the parent called navigability. Must NOT be claimed: that basin share predicts efficiency for other climbers or evaluators (one climber, one evaluator family, 4 tables); that local improvement probability is irrelevant within an encoding family.
